coverage_summary: NO-GO. Two residual High blockers remain; no Critical blocker found. The other contract items are explicit. Phase 6 does prevent premature hardware implementation: the master limits the current cook handoff to Phases 1–5, Phase 7 is explicitly BLOCKED_PENDING_PHASE_6, and Phase 6 must rewrite exact Phase 7/8 paths/procedures and rerun deep validation/red-team before hardware cook.

findings.title: Certificate and relay-verifier rollback binding remains incomplete
findings.summary: The protected profile does not explicitly bind the exact transmitted client chain or its client-issuer trust material, while relay CA/verifier and denylist state are only external versioned manifests. Replaying previously valid client and relay-side trust/revocation inputs can therefore restore retired or revoked authorization without violating the protected fields currently enumerated.

locations.role: Mounted chain is outside KMS and omitted from the enumerated protected profile fields
Canonical profile/floor steps do not add exact chain and issuer binding
Relay verifier and denylist are merely external versioned manifests
Negative injection omits old relay-verifier/denylist manifest replay

evidence.label: Execution path
evidence.explanation: Mounted client-chain inputs and external relay manifests are replayable configuration sources; the signer and relay can each accept an older mutually compatible state.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: A protected denylist version does not prove which verifier/denylist version the external relay enforces, and SPKI/serial/NodeId do not uniquely bind the exact leaf-first chain.

evidence.label: Minimal correction
evidence.explanation: Bind hashes/count/order of every exact client-chain DER entry and client-issuer profile into the protected active-profile digest. Require signed relay verifier/denylist manifests with an independently persisted monotonic version/digest floor, atomic fail-closed activation/recovery, enforced-version binding during registration, and explicit old-manifest replay tests on both sides.

findings.title: Production qualification is not bound to the exact qualified runtime tuple
findings.summary: The plan adds a separate protected ProductionQualified latch, but the signed qualification record has no frozen schema or requirement to bind and continuously match the exact silicon/board, RoT firmware, AP measurement, KMS/provider/image, policy, and production profile. A prior record or retained latch can survive a bound-component change and authorize a configuration reviewers never qualified.

locations.role: Qualification is an enum/latch without a qualified tuple
Firmware, profile, and latch are separate protected fields without binding semantics
Signed record lacks schema, trust root, freshness, and tuple binding
Runtime provenance is only recorded as evidence
Activation does not require protected equality checks against all live tuple values

evidence.label: Dangerous sink
evidence.explanation: ProductionQualified directly enables the durable production signing path.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: Independent signing and protected activation do not state what is signed, which protected key verifies it, or that every qualified-component change invalidates the latch.

evidence.label: Minimal correction
evidence.explanation: Freeze a canonical qualification record and protected reviewer trust root in Phase 6. Bind product/silicon/board identity, lifecycle, RoT firmware, AP measurement, KMS/provider and image hashes, protocol/policy/key generations, exact active profile digest, and a monotonic qualification epoch. Require protected verification against live values before every production sign, replay rejection, and automatic reversion to QualificationTest after any bound value changes.
